title: Liverpool vs. Man Utd Combined XI: Reds Dominate Fierce Rivals
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack6:00 PM ESTAlexander Isak (left) and Bruno Fernandes will take center stage at Anfield. / Steve Bardens - AMA/Getty Images (Isak), Dan Mullan/Getty Images (Fernandes)Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure begins at a daunting environment for the Argentine, with Liverpool’s cauldron welcoming the Red Devils to Merseyside on Sunday.
While United have found a way to compete at Anfield since succumbing to a 7–0 beatdown in 2023, even claiming victory under Ruben Amorim last season, Pochettino’s record at Liverpool is wretched.

There’s an acceptance that the new manager is inheriting no quick fix, with the current group of players at his disposal seemingly not cut to appease Pochettino’s demands. There’s certainly some quality to work with, but few would suggest Andoni Iraola is worse off on the personnel front, as he prepares to face another Marcelo Bielsa acolyte.
Considering all the players available for selection, here are Sports Illustrated’s thoughts on a combined XI between the two fierce rivals.

Alisson is one of the Premier League’s greatest goalkeepers. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesAlisson may no longer be performing at the level he once was, with injuries perhaps taking their toll.

Still, the Brazilian is one of the greatest goalkeepers in Premier League history, and he continues to offer glimpses of a more imperious past, with his outstanding save to deny Arsenal’s Christos Tzolis earlier this month a prime example.

Liverpool supporters are falling in love with a loan player. / Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesA collection of Man Utd managers has found Diogo Dalot irresistible, but we’re going in a different direction.

All of Liverpool’s recognized right backs are either injured or on the comeback trail. It’s been a real problem area for the Reds since Trent Alexander-Arnold left for Real Madrid, but fortunately, Iraola has stumbled upon a solution.

Supporters are often reminded to never fall in love with a loan player, yet Ronald Araújo has rendered that impossible since rocking up from Barcelona. His deployment as the Vinícius Júnior neutralizer in Catalonia has certainly come in handy for the Reds.

Jacquet has been an immediate hit. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesSometimes, it doesn’t take long at all to discern whether a player, in the words of Harry Redknapp, is “heading right to the very top.”

Jérémy Jacquet is one such player, having signed from Rennes in January and joining Liverpool in the summer. The young French defender is the archetypal modern-day center back, combining stellar possession play with all the defensive fundamentals one could possibly require. He exudes calm every time he takes to the field.

Van Dijk makes his 350th Premier League appearance on Sunday. /  Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesVirgil van Dijk is an injury doubt, but is nonetheless expected to make his 350th Premier League appearance on Sunday.

Like Alisson, the Dutchman may not be what he once was, with mental lapses increasing in frequency. The otherworldly consistency of his apex has faded, yet Van Dijk is still capable of producing dominant defensive displays well into his twilight.
Shaw’s injury woes have returned. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesOh, hello Man Utd. Welcome to the party!
In truth, we’re not exactly sure whether Luke Shaw will be available to Pochettino on Merseyside after a six-week absence, but he has trained ahead of Sunday’s encounter.

Given Liverpool’s options, Shaw finds his place in the team. He was instrumental in Man Utd’s ascent under Michael Carrick last season, and his absence has proven costly so far this term—due to the club’s decision not to sign an able deputy in the summer.
Mac Allister is playing for a new contract. /  Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesThe Argentine’s form nose dived in 2025–26, hence why Alexis Mac Allister is yet to extend his contract on Merseyside.

However, Mac Allister has performed this season like a man desperate to put pen to paper. While Iraola has chopped and changed in his engine room, the bitty Argentine has remained a constant, popping up with a goal or two from midfield.

Szoboszlai’s best work at Anfield has come in a more advanced midfield role. / John Walton/PA Images/Getty ImagesDominik Szoboszlai certainly hasn’t showcased his best stuff in 2026–27, but neither has any of Man Utd’s midfield operators.
